title: Session 4 – Text and Data Mining + Visual Mining

blocks.text: Text and data mining (TDM) turn large volumes of mostly unstructured data into insights. Companies like Coca-Cola monitor and analyse social media mentions in real time (more than 30 mentions per minute in English alone).
Text mining treats unstructured text. Typical algorithms:
children: Stemming/lemmatization: reduce words to their root
TF-IDF: frequency and weight of a term
Named Entity Recognition: identify names, locations etc.
Opinion mining/sentiment analysis: positive, negative, neutral
Topic modelling & text classification: hidden themes, predefined labels

blocks.text: Text mining success depends on data quality (garbage in, garbage out), data cleansing, algorithm selection, scalability, model evaluation and ethical boundaries.
Data mining uncovers meaningful patterns or rules:
children: Association rule mining: relationships among items
Classification: predict categorical labels from training data
Sequential pattern mining: sequences, time series, transactions
Anomaly detection: unusual patterns, e.g. fraud

blocks.text: Predictive analytics uses historical data with statistical modelling, data mining and machine learning – for demand forecasting, supply chain optimisation, fraud detection, predicting customer behaviour, healthcare diagnostics and stock markets.

Sentiment analysis supports brand reputation monitoring, customer research and feedback, market research, crisis prevention and management, customer service and social media/financial/political analysis (examples: Boeing after the China Eastern crash; cryptocurrency price prediction).
Visual mining extracts insights from images and videos (Dash Hudson Vision AI, YouScan). More than 80% of visual imagery is untapped; it helps to spot emerging trends and monitor competitors.

Team activity (Brand24, Microsoft vs Apple): compare volume of mentions, social and non-social reach, positive and negative mentions, and the sentiment ratio = positive / negative mentions – then explain which events could have driven the results.
A branch of analytics that encompasses the treatment of unstructured text information.
The exploration and analysis of data to uncover patterns or rules that are meaningful.
Advanced analytics that makes predictions about future outcomes using historical data combined with statistical modelling, data mining techniques and machine learning.
The process of identifying and assessing what is being said about a company, individual, product or brand on the internet.
The process of analysing online text to determine its emotional tone – positive, negative or neutral.
Extracting trends, patterns, insights and knowledge from visual data with data mining, computer vision and data visualisation.
The revision session mentioned sentiment analysis as a possible exam exercise – practise computing and interpreting sentiment ratios together with reach and volume.
